'''Norchad Bascom Omier Rojas''' (born 28 August 2001) is a Nicaraguan professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas State Red Wolves men's basketball|Arkansas State Red Wolves]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] and [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]].

==Early life==
A native of [[Bluefields]], Nicaragua, Omier grew up playing several sports, including [[baseball]]. He started playing [[basketball]] by the age of 13 after a local coach noticed his height.<ref name="fiba">{{cite web |title=Norchad Omier keeps Nicaragua's basketball dreams alive |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/norchad-omier-keeps-nicaragua-s-basketball-dreams-alive |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=4 November 2021 |date=1 September 2021}}</ref> Omier trained at La Academica de Basketball Bluefields in his hometown. He explored professional opportunities in Mexico before joining Miami Prep in [[Miami|Miami, Florida]] on a full scholarship.<ref name="lederman">{{cite web |last1=Lederman |first1=Eli |title=Pride of a country: Omier forges Nicaragua’s hoops identity |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/feb/18/pride-of-a-country/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=4 November 2021 |date=18 February 2021}}</ref> Omier averaged 26.7 points and 20.3 rebounds per game, and recorded 40 points and 17 rebounds against [[IMG Academy]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lorensen |first1=Nick |title=From Bluefields, Nicaragua to Freshman Phenomenon: The Story of Norchad Omier |url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2021/2/26/22297024/norchad-omier-arkansas-state-red-wolves-freshman-of-the-year-sun-belt-conference |website=Mid-Major Madness |access-date=4 November 2021 |date=26 February 2021}}</ref> He committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Arkansas State Red Wolves men's basketball|Arkansas State]] over offers from [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]], [[Mercer Bears men's basketball|Mercer]], [[UMBC Retrievers men's basketball|UMBC]] and [[Marist Red Foxes men's basketball|Marist]], and became the first Nicaraguan to sign an [[NCAA Division I]] basketball scholarship.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Reed |first1=Jeff |title=Red Wolves add commitment {{sic|from f|rom|nolink=y}} Central America |url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas-state/Article/Red-Wolves-add-commitment-from-from-Central-America--145675958/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=4 November 2021 |date=3 April 2020}}</ref> He joined the Red Wolves under Spanish-speaking head coach [[Mike Balado]]. <ref>{{cite web |last1=Turbeville |first1=Kevin |title=A-State's Omier learning game quickly |url=https://www.jonesborosun.com/sports/a-states-omier-learning-game-quickly/article_a45b4a16-c40b-563c-8e8e-6ab88b5a117d.html |website=Jonesboro Sun |access-date=4 November 2021 |date=4 February 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
On 16 January 2021, Omier posted a freshman season-high 22 points and 17 rebounds in a 93–72 win against [[Louisiana–Monroe Warhawks men's basketball|Louisiana–Monroe]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Omier carries Arkansas St. over Louisiana-Monroe 93-72 |url=https://www.si.com/college/college-basketball/game/2277265 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=4 November 2021 |date=16 January 2021}}</ref> As a freshman, he averaged 12.6 points and 12.3 rebounds per game, earning First Team All-[[Sun Belt Conference|Sun Belt]] and Freshman of the Year honors. Omier became the fourth Division I freshman since the [[1992–93 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|1992–93 season]] to average at least 12 points and 12 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Garner |first1=Caleb |last2=Taylor |first2=Mark |title=Omier named Sun Belt Preseason Player of the Year, Eaton and Washington also named to all-SBC team |url=https://www.kait8.com/2021/10/21/omier-named-sun-belt-preseason-player-year-eaton-washington-also-named-all-sbc-team/?outputType=apps |website=[[KAIT]] |access-date=4 November 2021 |date=21 October 2021}}</ref> At the conclusion of the 2021-22 regular season, Omier was named [[Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Sun Belt Player of the Year]] and Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arkansas State forward Norchad Omier named SBC Player of the Year & Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.kait8.com/2022/02/28/arkansas-state-forward-norchad-omier-named-sbc-player-year-defensive-player-year/ |access-date=28 February 2022 |work=[[KAIT]] |date=28 February 2022}}</ref> He transferred to [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] and averaged 13.1 points and 10 rebounds per game as a junior.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Benjamin |first1=Marcus |title=Norchad Omier on track for a historic finish to the 2023-2024 season |url=https://miami.rivals.com/news/norchad-omier-on-track-for-a-historic-finish-to-the-2023-2024-season |access-date=14 March 2024 |work=[[Rivals.com]] |date=31 December 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career== 
===Cleveland Charge (2025–2026)===
After going undrafted in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Omier joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavs Announce 2025 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-summer-league-roster-250703|website=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2025|access-date=July 11, 2025}}</ref> He was waived by the Cavaliers, but was then added to the training camp roster of their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Cleveland Charge]].<ref>{{cite news|title= Cleveland Charge 2025 Training Camp Roster |url= https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2025-training-camp-roster |access-date=November 7, 2025 |work=[[NBA G League]] |date=October 25, 2025}}</ref> 

During the [[2025–26 NBA G League season]], Omier established himself as one of the most consistent and productive frontcourt players in the league. In 27 games, he averaged 19.3 points, 12.3 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game while shooting 58.9% from the field.<ref>{{cite web|title=Norchad Omier and Sean Pedulla Named to 2025–26 NBA G League All-Rookie Team|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/norchad-omier-and-sean-pedulla-named-to-2025-26-nba-g-league-all-rookie-team/n-6344884|website=OurSports Central|date=April 7, 2026|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref> He led all qualified rookies in rebounds per game (12.3) and total offensive rebounds, while finishing among the league leaders in total rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=Norchad Omier and Sean Pedulla Named to 2025–26 NBA G League All-Rookie Team|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/norchad-omier-and-sean-pedulla-named-to-2025-26-nba-g-league-all-rookie-team/n-6344884|website=OurSports Central|date=April 7, 2026|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref> Omier scored in double figures in all 27 games and recorded 27 double-doubles across the regular season and Tip-Off Tournament.<ref>{{cite web|title=Norchad Omier and Sean Pedulla Named to 2025–26 NBA G League All-Rookie Team|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/norchad-omier-and-sean-pedulla-named-to-2025-26-nba-g-league-all-rookie-team/n-6344884|website=OurSports Central|date=April 7, 2026|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref>

Omier was named NBA G League Player of the Week for games played from February 2–8, 2026, after averaging 26.0 points, 15.5 rebounds, and 4.0 assists.<ref>{{cite web|title=Norchad Omier named NBA G League Player of the Week|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/norchad-omier-named-nba-g-league-player-of-the-week|website=NBA G League|date=February 10, 2026|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref> His performance throughout the season earned him selection to the [[NBA G League Next Up Game]] during NBA All-Star 2026. On April 7, 2026, he was named to the All-NBA G League Rookie Team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Norchad Omier and Sean Pedulla Named to 2025–26 NBA G League All-Rookie Team|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/norchad-omier-and-sean-pedulla-named-to-2025-26-nba-g-league-all-rookie-team/n-6344884|website=OurSports Central|date=April 7, 2026|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref>

Omier also finished third in voting for the 2025–26 Kia NBA G League Rookie of the Year award.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA G League announces Rookie of the Year winner, runner-ups|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/nba-rookies/nba-g-league-announces-rookie-of-the-year-winner-runner-ups|website=Sports Illustrated|date=April 2, 2026|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref>

===Los Angeles / San Diego Clippers (2026)===
Following his strong G League campaign, Omier signed a two-way contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] during the 2025–26 season, allowing him to split time between the NBA roster and the [[San Diego Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Norchad Omier player profile|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/1641807/|website=NBA G League|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref> Omier made his NBA debut on March 2, 2026, becoming the first Nicaraguan-born player to appear in an NBA game. In his initial appearances, he demonstrated efficiency in limited minutes, contributing in scoring, rebounding, and interior defense.<ref>{{cite web|title=Norchad Omier NBA stats|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4702134/norchad-omier|website=ESPN|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref>

Throughout his rookie season, Omier gained recognition for his physical playing style, rebounding ability, and high motor. His style of play drew comparisons in basketball media to former NBA forward [[Charles Barkley]] due to his undersized but powerful presence in the paint.<ref>{{cite web|title=Norchad Omier dubbed “G League’s Charles Barkley”|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DVb34tBkgOE/|website=Instagram|publisher=GTV Hoops / NBA G League collaboration|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref>

His consistent statistical production also led to him being described in media coverage as a "double-double machine." Off the court, Omier experienced a rapid rise in popularity, with his jersey selling out at the official Los Angeles Clippers team store shortly after release, reflecting strong fan demand.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jerseys de Norchad Omier se agotan en tienda oficial de Clippers|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DWPoR7Mj6Vx/|website=Instagram|publisher=CuadranteMX|access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
In April 2021, Omier made his [[Nicaragua men's national basketball team|national team]] debut for Nicaragua during [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Americas)#Pre-Qualifiers|2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification]].<ref name="lederman2">{{cite web |last1=Lederman |first1=Eli |title=Omier to represent Nicaragua in event |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/apr/08/omier-to-represent-nicaragua-in-event/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=4 November 2021 |date=8 April 2021}}</ref>
